title: Read a lymph-node section from outside inward

regions.label: Surrounding pale tissue
regions.observation: Large pale polygonal spaces with thin boundaries surround the denser lymphoid tissue.
regions.interpretation: These are consistent with adipose tissue outside the node. Establish the organ boundary before treating pale spaces as internal lymphatic channels.
regions.limit: A pale space alone does not identify a sinus.

regions.label: Peripheral nodular pattern
regions.observation: Rounded, more densely stained lymphoid profiles are arranged toward the periphery.
regions.interpretation: Compare their relationship to the outer boundary and intervening tissue. Follicular architecture supports a cortical compartment.
regions.limit: This overview cannot assign each nucleus to a B-cell subtype or establish a germinal-centre reaction in every profile.

regions.label: Heterogeneous inner regions
regions.observation: Inner tissue has a different mixture of dense areas, pale spaces and vascular-looking profiles.
regions.interpretation: Orient an inner compartment, then request a more detailed view before separating medullary cords, sinuses, vessels and adipose spaces.
regions.limit: Do not label every pale space a medullary sinus; lining and contents must be inspected.

regions.label: Whole-organ argument
regions.observation: Peripheral nodules and a differently organized interior occur inside a distinct tissue boundary with surrounding fat.
regions.interpretation: Combine those relationships with the creator-provided normal lymph-node provenance. A single follicle would not distinguish node from spleen or mucosal lymphoid tissue.
regions.limit: The specimen is a section through an organ, not a live map of lymph flow, and its entire three-dimensional hilum is not demonstrated.

model: The outer boundary separates denser lymphoid tissue from surrounding adipose tissue. Rounded peripheral profiles differ from the heterogeneous interior. These relationships support the creator-identified lymph-node interpretation. A higher-power, documented preparation is needed to resolve individual cell types and distinguish each inner vessel from a sinus.
